Cautiously hawkish read. The FOMC raised the target range to 4.75–5%, lifted IOER to 4.9%, and kept balance-sheet runoff on course while noting that recent banking stresses will likely tighten credit. The Fed’s Financial Stability Report reinforces this assessment: it highlights persistent inflation and monetary tightening as prominent risks, along with market liquidity strains and volatility, and notes that higher rates weigh on credit quality. While the system is described as sound and resilient, the FSR’s Survey of Salient Risks and its discussion of tightening financial conditions point to a negative skew for growth and hiring beyond the immediate 25 bp hike. Standing facilities help contain instability but do not dilute the restrictive stance aimed at disinflation. Net tone: modestly more negative than neutral with a disinflationary tilt.
